clue.text: Pub on Merseyside initially provides humour

parts.note: PH is the map abbreviation for a public house
in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

indicators.note: 'initially' means at the start, so only the opening letter of the word before it is wanted

parts.note: first letter of Merseyside

explanation.surface: A Liverpool pub where the banter keeps everyone laughing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' looks like a joining word but is the cricket term: the on side of the field is the leg side, giving LEG. PH + LEG + M = PHLEGM.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval medicine held four bodily humours, and phlegm was one of them, thought to cause a calm, sluggish temperament.

clue.text: God took drugs

parts.note: had = took, as in 'had a biscuit'
E is ecstasy, so Es are ecstasy tablets

explanation.walkthrough: E for ecstasy is a crossword staple, and its plural Es stands for 'drugs'. HAD + ES = HADES.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Hades is the ruler of the underworld, brother of Zeus, and his name also came to mean the realm itself.

clue.text: Old books, I see, are unusual objects

parts.note: ex = former, old
OT = Old Testament, a set of books
I as printed
C sounds like 'see'; also c. for circa is not it here, just the letter C that sounds like the word
an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A

explanation.surface: A collector remarks on the strange curiosities to be found among old books.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word before the definition is a small piece: 'see' gives the letter C, and 'are' is the metric unit of area (100 square metres), abbreviated A.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotica is a plural noun for strange, foreign or striking things, so it matches a collection of odd curios.

clue.text: Honour royal, ignoring no good President

parts.note: MBE = Member of the Order of the British Empire, an honour

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so letters are dropped

parts.note: a king is a royal
NG is the abbreviation for no good; these letters go

explanation.surface: Someone snubs a royal honour because they rate it no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No good' reads as an opinion of the honour but is a standard two-letter abbreviation. The MBE is a British honour given by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Thabo Mbeki succeeded Nelson Mandela as the head of state of South Africa, serving from 1999 to 2008.

clue.text: Instigated raunchy frolic in private with Duke

indicators.note: 'with' means alongside, so one piece simply follows another
being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece is enclosed by another

parts.note: Pte is the abbreviation for the army rank of private
a romp is a frolic, often a raunchy one
D = Duke

explanation.surface: A tabloid scandal about a duke's saucy private romp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In private' reads as 'secretly', but private is the soldier's rank, abbreviated in army lists. 'Raunchy' is not an anagram hint, just colour for the frolic.
explanation.definitionFit: To prompt something is to cause or provoke it, so prompted is a past-tense synonym for set in motion.

clue.text: Crook headhunts pastor to solicit donations

indicators.note: as a verb, to crook is to bend, so the letters are bent out of shape

parts.note: anagram fodder, fifteen letters

explanation.surface: A dodgy recruiter poaches a vicar to run his fundraising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crook' looks like a noun, the villain of the piece; it is the verb 'bend'. The two long words hold exactly the fifteen letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes collecting money informally by passing a hat among a group, so it means asking people to give.

clue.text: Like some beer, as gonad hurt badly

indicators.note: something done badly is messed up, so the letters come out in disorder

parts.note: anagram fodder, nine letters

explanation.surface: A comic image of a painful injury below the belt.
explanation.walkthrough: The anatomy is pure fodder; 'as' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer served from a cask or keg through a tap, rather than a bottle or can, is described with this phrase.

clue.text: President Trump primarily working in northern city

parts.note: Pres. is the abbreviation for President

indicators.note: 'primarily' means first of all, so the word's opening letter is taken

parts.note: first letter of Trump
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: The US president is off on a working visit to a city in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface wants a presidential trip, but 'President' is only an abbreviation. PRES + T + ON = PRESTON.
explanation.definitionFit: Preston is the administrative centre of Lancashire, in the north-west of England, granted city status in 2002.

clue.text: Periodically sell Littler as the crème de la crème

indicators.note: something that happens periodically recurs at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the even-placed letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Marketing darts champion Luke Littler as the very best in the game.
explanation.walkthrough: Luke Littler is a young English darts world champion, so the surface reads as sports marketing. Take the 2nd, 4th, 6th, 8th and 10th letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means the cream of the cream, the very best of a group, which is exactly the select top tier.

clue.text: Moved head up and down, right to left, and peeled vegetable

indicators.note: right to left means read the word backwards
peeled means the outer skin is gone, so the first and last letters are dropped

parts.note: to nod is to move the head up and down, so this is nodded

explanation.surface: Someone nods along and then peels a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peeled' strips the outer letters of NODDED to leave ODDE, and 'right to left' reads that backwards. Either order of the two steps gives the same result.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddo is another name for taro, a starchy tropical root vegetable.

clue.text: Sex seen on simple browsers? Take care

indicators.note: in an across clue, to be on something is to come after it, so this piece is placed last

parts.note: easy = simple
does are female deer, which browse on leaves
'it' is an old euphemism for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: A warning about explicit content turning up on basic web browsers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Browsers' suggests web software, but they are animals that browse on leaves. Using 'it' for sex is an old euphemism setters love.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are phrases urging someone to proceed gently and cautiously, so the idiom and the instruction match.

clue.text: After reflecting, one declines to go into Vauxhall plant

indicators.note: going into something means being placed inside it

parts.note: the Astra is a Vauxhall car model

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror is flipped, so the letters come out backwards

parts.note: I = one, and dips = declines

explanation.surface: Someone thinks it over and turns down a job at the Vauxhall car plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like the factory of the surface but is the definition. Vauxhall is a British car maker, and the insertion goes after the first letter of the model name.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspidistra is a hardy leafy houseplant, famously common in Victorian and Edwardian British parlours.

clue.text: Tramp and care worker taking back boxes

indicators.note: taken back means going the other way, so the letters read backwards
to box something is to enclose it, so the letters sit inside the words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A homeless man and the care worker who takes him in.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed letters lie in 'worKER Taking'; read backwards they spell TREK. 'Boxes' is the hidden indicator, not something being carried.
explanation.definitionFit: As verbs, to tramp and to trek both mean to walk a long, tiring distance on foot.

clue.text: Party leader in Brighton meeting Prime Minister, briefly, for fight

indicators.note: made brief means cut short, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its front, so only the opening letter counts

parts.note: first letter of Brighton
Clement Attlee, Labour Prime Minister 1945-51

explanation.surface: The Labour Party conference in Brighton, where the leader meets a former Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Attlee was the post-war Labour Prime Minister; cut short he loses his last E. Brighton is a seaside town that hosts party conferences.
explanation.definitionFit: To do battle is an idiom for engaging in combat, so the phrase is a verb matching the verb 'fight'.

clue.text: Manufacturer of stock line of game that's inconclusive

definitions.meaning: a British brand of stock cubes
in noughts and crosses a row of nought, cross, nought wins for no one

explanation.walkthrough: Oxo is a British brand of stock cubes. Noughts and crosses is the British name for tic-tac-toe, and a mixed line of O, X, O decides nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a trade name for gravy cubes; the other is a literal row of marks in the pencil game that fails to win.

clue.text: Permit revolutionary to come up with cycling broadcast

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned around, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to let is to permit

indicators.note: cycling means letters go round, the first letter moving to the end

parts.note: to devise is to come up with an idea

explanation.surface: A permit is issued for a revolutionary to take part in a cycling event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' reverses LET to TEL; 'cycling' sends the D of DEVISE to the back, giving EVISED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something televised is transmitted on television, so broadcast in the past-participle sense.

clue.text: Man loves penguin

parts.note: a gent is a man
love is zero in tennis, and zero looks like O

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a man doting on a bird; 'loves' is two tennis zeros. GENT + OO = GENTOO.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentoo is a species of penguin with a white band across its head, found around Antarctica.

clue.text: I smell from the bottom, a fetish

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from the bottom means going upward, the wrong way

parts.note: I as printed
BO = body odour

explanation.surface: A crude confession about a smell from someone's rear end.
explanation.walkthrough: Written upward, I + BO becomes OBI. 'Fetish' sounds like a kink but is the charm or talisman sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Obi, or obeah, is a Caribbean form of folk magic, and also a charm used in it, which is the old sense of fetish.

clue.text: Without fuel supply? It's terrible

parts.note: w/o is the abbreviation for without

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, it means bendily, so the letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone laments being cut off from their energy supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' is a noun in the surface but the adverb from supple, meaning in a supple way, so it bends the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Woeful and terrible both describe something very bad or of shockingly poor quality.

clue.text: Dancer lying about conviction, yet no further checks?

indicators.note: 'about' means turned around, so the letters are read backwards
to check is to hold back or contain, so the letters are held inside the words

parts.note: the letters span the last of the first word, two whole words and the start of the last

explanation.surface: A dancer lies about a criminal conviction, hoping nobody looks any deeper.
explanation.walkthrough: Read convictioN YET NO Further backwards to get FONTEYN. 'Checks' sounds like background checks but is the hiding instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Margot Fonteyn was a celebrated English prima ballerina of the Royal Ballet, famous for her partnership with Nureyev.

clue.text: Gold top is returned by American getting stiff examination

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
as printed

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: as printed
A = American

explanation.surface: A US examiner gives a gold-medal performance a rigorous testing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stiff' reads as 'tough' but is slang for a corpse. Only IS turns round, then A is added after it.
explanation.definitionFit: An autopsia, a rarer form of autopsy, is a post-mortem, and a stiff is slang for a dead body.

clue.text: Phosphorus and toxic heavy metal (not thorium) found in ancient garment

parts.note: P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus

indicators.note: 'not' excludes something, so those letters are left out

parts.note: thallium is a highly poisonous heavy metal
Th is the chemical symbol for thorium; these letters go

explanation.surface: A chemistry report on poisonous elements detected in an old robe.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole surface is chemistry: P + THALLIUM without TH = PALLIUM.
explanation.definitionFit: The pallium was a large rectangular cloak worn by men in ancient Greece and Rome, like a Greek himation.

clue.text: Perhaps Polanski's first to flee country

indicators.note: when the first runs away, the opening letter is gone

parts.note: the film director's first name; 'Perhaps' flags a definition by example

explanation.surface: The film director Roman Polanski famously fled the United States in 1978.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface alludes to Polanski's real flight from America. His first name ROMAN loses its R.
explanation.definitionFit: Oman is a sultanate on the south-east coast of the Arabian Peninsula, a sovereign state.

clue.text: Child about to leave Spanish island

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: Minorca (Menorca) is a Balearic island
ca. = circa, about; these letters go

explanation.surface: A child is about to leave a Spanish island after a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'on the point of'; 'about' is really CA, removed from MINORCA.
explanation.definitionFit: In law a minor is a person below the age of majority, so the word is a formal term for a young person.

clue.text: Palace revises all manoeuvres

indicators.note: a manoeuvre moves things into new positions, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, ten letters

explanation.surface: Buckingham Palace, perhaps, rethinks all its tactical moves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manoeuvres' looks like a plural noun but is the verb acting on the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Versailles is the vast royal palace built by Louis XIV outside Paris, the seat of the French court.

clue.text: Indo-European fairly regularly meeting Asian on vacation

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every second letter is picked out

parts.note: the even letters of fairly

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so only the outside letters remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of Asian

explanation.surface: A European traveller quite often runs into an Asian one while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fairly' reads as 'somewhat' but is fodder; 'on vacation' means emptied, not away on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: In linguistics Aryan was an old name for the Indo-Iranian branch of the language family, so the terms overlap.

clue.text: Wear down staff in telecommunications company

indicators.note: 'in' places one thing inside another

parts.note: EE is a British mobile phone network
a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: Management at a phone company grinds its employees down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' suggests employees but is a stick. The company is EE, a UK mobile network, whose two letters wrap round the stick.
explanation.definitionFit: To erode is to wear away gradually, as water and wind do to rock, which matches wear down as a verb.

clue.text: Substitute duty nurse working around Germany

indicators.note: going around something encloses it
something working is in operation, so the letters are set into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, nine letters
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A relief nurse is on shift in a German hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters wrap around D, the vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland), placed after UN.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre an understudy learns a role so they can stand in for the regular performer, so it is a stand-in.

clue.text: Charged particle installing resistance in metal

indicators.note: to install something is to put it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: an ion is an electrically charged particle
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A physics lesson on a charged particle creating resistance in a metal conductor.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all physics, and the answer is the metal it mentions: I(R)ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron is a common metallic element, symbol Fe, used to make steel.

clue.text: Type of jazz covers popular with brides, essentially, in Caribbean island

indicators.note: a cover goes over and around, so one piece wraps the others

parts.note: trad is short for traditional jazz
in = fashionable, popular

indicators.note: the essence of something is its core, so the central letters are taken

parts.note: the two middle letters of brides

explanation.surface: A trad jazz band plays cover versions that go down well at Caribbean weddings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covers' looks like cover versions of songs but means wrapping around; the jazz word encloses both the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Trinidad is the larger of the two main islands making up the nation of Trinidad and Tobago in the West Indies.

clue.text: Piece of music, the last from Jocelyn Brown

indicators.note: the last from a word is its closing letter, so only that one is taken

parts.note: last letter of Jocelyn
umber is a brown earth pigment

explanation.surface: Singer Jocelyn Brown's latest track is released.
explanation.walkthrough: Jocelyn Brown is an American soul and dance singer, so the name looks whole; 'Brown' is the colour UMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: A number is a song or tune performed as one item in a show or on an album, so a musical piece.
